cf.title: Optimize MCV stats for sortable types and utilize sorted-order properties

input.subject: Optimize MCV stats for sortable types and utilize sorted-order properties

verdict_reasoning: The proposal fails at level 1b on maintenance-fit-1, already-exists-1 and demand-1. The author's release-build reruns show scalar = and < planning 5 to 6 percent slower than master, and the join gain was measured only with the hash threshold raised to 202. No workload in the thread shows planning time lost in MCV scans. v16 adds a sixth pg_statistic slot and duplicates MCV data for all users, so the benefit must be shown first.

brief.title: Store MCV lists in value order to speed up selectivity estimation
brief.problem: The planner scans the frequency-ordered MCV list linearly, calling the comparison function for each entry, when it estimates equality, inequality and join selectivity. The author wants to cut this planner CPU cost, mainly for large statistics targets and expensive comparisons such as long text with a nondeterministic collation.
brief.proposed_design: ANALYZE stores a new statistics kind, STATISTIC_KIND_MCV_VALUE_SORTED (8), that holds the MCV pairs in ascending value order. The planner uses endpoint checks, binary search and merge matching in var_eq_const(), mcv_selectivity(), eqjoinsel() and the range helpers. Up to v15, kind 8 replaced kind 1 for sortable types; v16 keeps both kinds and raises STATISTIC_NUM_SLOTS from five to six.
user_visible_surface: New statistics kind 8, STATISTIC_KIND_MCV_VALUE_SORTED, in pg_statistic; extensions reading MCV slots see it.
v16: STATISTIC_NUM_SLOTS goes from 5 to 6, adding stakind6/staop6/stacoll6/stanumbers6/stavalues6-style catalog columns.
v16: new most_common_vals_value_sorted and most_common_freqs_value_sorted columns in pg_stats and pg_stats_ext_exprs; v15 instead reordered the existing columns.
Optional most_common_vals_kind parameter for pg_restore_attribute_stats() and the expr arguments of pg_restore_extended_stats() (v8 to v15); v16 imports a kind 1 and kind 8 pair.
New C function get_attstatsslot_mcv() for explicit MCV representation selection; pg_dump and postgres_fdw statistics export change.
author_claims: ANALYZE overhead is about 2 to 3 percent in the author's tests.
Release-build reruns show join planning time about 14 to 16 percent faster with v16, using a hash threshold of 202.
Release builds show scalar = and < cases about 5 to 6 percent slower than master; earlier 40 to 60 percent gains came from debug builds.
Plans and row estimates match master in the tested cases; v15 had a join estimate defect that v16 fixes.
v16 touches 27 files, with about 3,400 inserted lines.
brief.thread_state: Only Ilia Evdokimov replied, arguing the MCV scan is cheap at normal targets, a new statistics kind wastes slots, and the status quo is better. The author has posted 16 versions alone and now asks whether the paired design with a sixth slot is acceptable.
unclear: The patch shows no benefit over master's default hash path for eqjoinsel(), which applies at the default threshold of 200.
The thread does not say how pg_upgrade or extensions handle the sixth slot and the changed pg_statistic layout.
The thread gives no measurement of planning time at large statistics targets in release builds, where the author expects the gain.
The thread does not show that real workloads spend enough planning time in MCV scans to justify duplicating MCV data.
The thread does not say how third-party consumers that read kind 1 behave under v16 when kind 8 also exists.
search_queries: most common values sorted by value

prior_attempts.title: ANALYZE: hash-accelerate MCV tracking for equality-only types
prior_attempts.reason: The visible messages do not show why. Ilia Evdokimov asked how often this narrow path runs, since most types use compute_scalar_stats(), and John Naylor questioned the threshold of 100. Both points were still open when the entry was withdrawn, on the day Ilia posted a cleanup review of v5 with no objection.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P2 sped up MCV tracking inside compute_distinct_stats() for equality-only types with no catalog change. This proposal changes the stored MCV form for sortable types, adds a sixth statistics slot and changes planner consumers.

objections.title: Permanent catalog change and duplicated MCV data for a gain not shown at defaults
objections.failure_scenario: Every installation stores two copies of each sortable column's MCV list and spends 2 to 3 percent more on every ANALYZE. Scalar = and < planning gets 5 to 6 percent slower in release builds. The only measured gain is on an eqjoinsel() path that the default hash threshold of 200 skips for 100+100 MCVs.
objections.argument: Message #29 retracts the debug-build speedups. It reports scalar regressions and join gains measured only at a hash threshold of 202, and calls the default-path benefit unproven. Message #7 argues the scan is cheap at normal targets, and no release data at large targets has answered that. Once STATISTIC_NUM_SLOTS is six and pg_stats has new columns, the project cannot take them back, so the costs fall on all users for a gain that is not yet demonstrated.
objections.author_must_show: In a release build at default settings, which real workload spends enough planning time in MCV scans that v16 gives a measurable net gain over master?

precedents.title: SIMD optimization for list_sort and tuple-sort

critic.reasoning: Messages #29 and #30 concede each point: scalar cases are slower, join gains are off the default path, and the costs are not yet justified. P4 concerns an external library and must not be used as support; new measurements could answer this, so fixable.

objections.title: Master's existing hash matching in eqjoinsel() already covers the measured join case
objections.failure_scenario: A user runs the default build with 100-entry MCV lists on both join sides, so master already takes the eqjoinsel() hash path. After upgrade they pay a sixth pg_statistic slot, duplicated MCV data and wider pg_stats, but planning time does not improve. Nobody sees this until someone benchmarks at the default threshold.
objections.argument: The only release-build gain shown is the join cases, which the author ran with the hash threshold raised to 202 to force the non-hash path (messages #29, #30). The author states the benefit over master's default hash path is unproven. The scalar = and < cases are 5 to 6 percent slower in release builds. So the gain found so far sits in a case master already handles with an existing mechanism, and the patch adds a second matching method for the same job.
objections.author_must_show: At the default hash threshold, which planning workloads become measurably faster with kind 8 than with master's existing eqjoinsel() hash path?

critic.reasoning: Message #29 says the join gain was measured with the hash threshold raised to 202 and is unproven against master's default hash path. A default-threshold or large-target measurement could answer this, and the hash path does not cover the scalar cases, so fixable.

objections.title: No shown workload where MCV scans cost noticeable planning time
objections.failure_scenario: A committer merges a large statistics change to speed up planning. Users on default settings then see scalar = and < planning about 5 to 6 percent slower. Join gains appear only on a non-default path, so after release nobody can point to a workload that got faster.
objections.argument: The thread has no field report, -general or -bugs thread, or production story about planner time spent in MCV scans. The only other participant, in message #7, called the scan cheap at normal targets and the status quo better. The author's release reruns in messages #29 and #30 show scalar cases slower than master. The join gains used hash threshold 202, and the author says a benefit over the default hash path is unproven. The large earlier gains came from debug builds.
objections.author_must_show: Which real workloads, measured on release builds at default settings or at large statistics targets, spend a significant share of planning time in MCV comparisons that v16 removes?

critic.reasoning: The thread has no field report or production workload, and the only other participant argued for the status quo in message #7. The "unclear" list in the brief confirms that no release measurement at large statistics targets exists.

other_surviving.title: Stored value order goes stale when the collation sort order changes
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user upgrades ICU or the OS, and the collation sort order of a text column changes. Kind 8 is no longer sorted under the new rules, so binary search misses existing MCVs and var_eq_const() treats them as non-MCV. Row estimates drop until the next ANALYZE, and an import of the old kind 8 may be rejected by the ordering check.
other_surviving.argument: Kind 1 matches values by equality only and does not depend on sort order. Kind 8 adds that dependency for every sortable column, including the nondeterministic collations the author targets (message #25). A histogram that is out of order only blurs a range estimate. A binary search miss on the MCV list changes an equality estimate from the MCV frequency to the non-MCV estimate. The proposal does not say how a collation version change is detected or handled.
other_surviving.author_must_show: What does the planner do with a kind 8 slot whose order no longer matches the current collation, and how does import handle it after an upgrade?

critic.reasoning: Histogram lookups in master already depend on stored sort order, which lowers the planner half of this concern. The import ordering check in message #30 is new, and the thread does not say what it does after a collation version change.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Sixth statistics slot changes pg_statistic layout and VacAttrStats for everyone
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A monitoring tool, or an extension that reads pg_statistic directly, looks for an MCV kind only in stakind1 to stakind5. On an array column that uses six slots under v16, kind 1 can land in slot 6, so the tool sees no MCV list. Nothing reports an error, and the missing data shows up only in wrong reports or estimates.
other_surviving.argument: Message #28 shows array columns already fill all five slots, and v16 adds kind 8 next to kind 1, so slot 6 will be used. The author's own diagnostic query in message #12 hardcodes stakind1..5, which is how many tools read the catalog. Raising STATISTIC_NUM_SLOTS also changes the size of VacAttrStats and the Form_pg_statistic columns, which custom typanalyze functions in extensions fill or read. The thread does not discuss either consumer, and message #29 states that the benefit does not yet justify these costs.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Which in-tree and known third-party consumers read stakindN or VacAttrStats slot arrays, and how does each behave when kind 1 sits in slot 6?

critic.reasoning: Message #28 confirms that array columns fill five slots, so v16 uses slot 6, and SQL that reads only stakind1..5 misses it silently. Extensions recompile for each major version, so the VacAttrStats size change is the weaker half.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Duplicate MCV payload grows pg_statistic, syscache memory and ANALYZE WAL
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A site with many long-text columns at a high statistics target runs ANALYZE. Each pg_statistic row now stores the MCV values twice, so TOAST size, WAL from ANALYZE and the per-backend syscache footprint grow. The site finds this as catalog bloat and higher backend memory, whether or not its planning gets faster.
other_surviving.argument: v16 stores kind 1 and kind 8 with the same value-frequency pairs (message #29). The case the author targets, long text with statistics target 10000 (messages #22 and #25), is the case where the duplicated array is largest. Message #30 says the relation does not double but gives no measurement of catalog size, WAL volume or syscache memory. The release-build results show no gain for scalar cases and an unproven gain over the default hash path, so all users would pay this cost for an uncertain return.
other_surviving.author_must_show: How much do pg_statistic size, ANALYZE WAL volume and per-backend syscache memory grow at default and high statistics targets, measured against master?

critic.reasoning: Message #30 confirms the duplicated MCV payload and gives no measurement of catalog size, WAL volume or syscache memory. The cost falls on every sortable column that has an MCV list, whether or not planning gets faster.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Sorted order could be derived at read time without a catalog change
other_surviving.failure_scenario: The project changes the pg_statistic layout, the statistics views and the import functions to persist an ordering that can be computed from kind 1. Extensions and tools that read stakind1..stakind5 by SQL do not see slot 6. They must adapt for no new information.
other_surviving.argument: Kind 8 holds the same value-frequency pairs as kind 1 in a different order (message #29). A sorted copy could be built once when the planner loads the slot, or cached per relation, which leaves the catalog and the dump format unchanged. The thread compares only the replace design and the pair design (message #28), and does not discuss deriving the order at read time.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Why is a sorted copy built when the statistics are loaded into planner memory not enough, given that kind 8 adds no information beyond kind 1?

critic.reasoning: Message #28 compares only the replace design and the pair design. Sorting on each planner load would add comparisons, but a cached sorted copy is a real alternative that the thread does not discuss.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

refuted.title: Derived planner data becomes a catalog, view and import contract
refuted.failure_scenario: A tool that copies statistics between servers reads pg_stats and calls pg_restore_attribute_stats() with the existing MCV arguments only. The column gets kind 1 without kind 8, or partial-update validation rejects the call. The user sees changed plans or import errors after a routine statistics copy.
refuted.argument: Message #30 says kind 8 holds exactly the kind 1 pairs, only reordered, so it carries no information that kind 1 lacks. v16 still adds a sixth slot, two view columns, pair validation in import, and changes to pg_dump and postgres_fdw (messages #29, #30). Sorting kind 1 when the planner loads the slot would leave every user-facing interface unchanged. The thread does not say why that cheaper form was ruled out.
refuted.author_must_show: Why can kind 8 not be built from kind 1 when the planner reads the slot, so that pg_statistic, pg_stats and the import functions stay unchanged?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-3, which asks the same read-time question. The failure scenario here is also weak: message #30 says import accepts kind 1 alone, and the planner then uses kind 1 as master does.

refuted.title: A sixth slot breaks SQL that enumerates stakind1 to stakind5
refuted.failure_scenario: A monitoring query or extension reads pg_statistic slots 1 to 5, as the query in message #12 does. On an array column with all slots in use, the MCV or another kind lands in slot 6. The query then returns no MCV, and nothing reports the error.
refuted.argument: Message #28 shows that array columns already fill all five slots, which is why v16 raises STATISTIC_NUM_SLOTS. The slot count has been part of the visible catalog shape for many releases, and outside code hardcodes it. The proposal does not say which slot kind 1 occupies when six are needed, or whether the order of kinds is kept stable for these readers.
refuted.author_must_show: Which slot does kind 1 take when six are filled, and how do existing queries on stakind1..5 keep finding the MCV list?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which covers the same slot 6 scenario and adds the VacAttrStats consumers.

refuted.title: Two stored MCV forms must stay in sync across every producer
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a new statistics producer, import path, or MCV consumer. It updates kind 1 and leaves kind 8 alone, or it reads kind 8 where the code needs frequency order. Estimates then differ by code path, and nothing fails until a user reports a bad plan.
refuted.argument: v16 already needs pair validation in import, pg_dump, postgres_fdw, both views, a new get_attstatsslot_mcv(), and a tie-breaking policy for imported frequency ties (message #30). Each later MCV-related feature has to make the same kind choice, and a reviewer can miss it. The proposal does not include a check that fails loudly when the pair gets out of sync.
refuted.author_must_show: What mechanism stops a future producer or consumer from writing or reading only one of the two MCV kinds without anyone noticing?

critic.reasoning: Message #30 says import rejects kind 8 alone and validates pairs, and message #9 shows ANALYZE replaces the whole row. A producer that writes only kind 1 leaves the planner on master's kind 1 path, and get_attstatsslot_mcv() makes the consumer's choice explicit.

refuted.title: Every installation pays for a gain few workloads would see
refuted.failure_scenario: After upgrading, every ANALYZE writes a second copy of each sortable column's MCV list and runs about 2 to 3 percent longer. Tools that read pg_statistic or select * from pg_stats see a sixth slot and new columns. Only plans with large targets or costly comparisons gain anything.
refuted.argument: v16 raises STATISTIC_NUM_SLOTS to six, duplicates the MCV payload, changes the pg_stats and pg_stats_ext_exprs result shapes, and changes statistics import, pg_dump and postgres_fdw (messages #29, #30). These costs fall on all users, but the stated target is large statistics targets and expensive comparisons such as long text with a nondeterministic collation. Message #30 says the costs still need to be justified by performance evidence. The thread does not yet show that this narrow group is large enough to justify a permanent catalog change.
refuted.author_must_show: How many users run statistics targets or comparison types where the measured planning gain outweighs the extra slot, the duplicated MCV data and the extra ANALYZE time?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1, which makes the same point about costs for all users against a narrow gain, with more detail from the release measurements.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: v16 raises STATISTIC_NUM_SLOTS to six, which changes the pg_statistic row layout; upgraded clusters carry only kind 1 until the next ANALYZE.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: ANALYZE writes each sortable column's MCV values twice, so its WAL volume grows.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: New statistics kind 8, a sixth slot in pg_statistic, and new columns in pg_stats and pg_stats_ext_exprs.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: STATISTIC_NUM_SLOTS and the VacAttrStats slot arrays change size, and a new get_attstatsslot_mcv() is added.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: var_eq_const(), mcv_selectivity(), eqjoinsel() and the range helpers get new lookup paths.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: pg_dump statistics export and pg_restore_attribute_stats() must carry and validate a kind 1 and kind 8 pair.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: New pg_stats columns must keep the existing privilege filter, and ordered lookups call the "<" operator on user data.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Two stored MCV forms, pair validation in import, and about 3,400 new lines across 27 files.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Selectivity estimation runs for every planned query; release builds show scalar cases 5 to 6 percent slower.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: Master's eqjoinsel() hash path already handles the join case at the default threshold of 200.

questions: In a release build at default settings, which workload plans measurably faster with v16 than with master, and by how much?
At the default hash threshold of 200, how does v16 join planning time compare with master's eqjoinsel() hash path?
What are the release-build planning times at large statistics targets, such as 10000 with long text under a nondeterministic collation?
Why is a sorted copy built from kind 1 when the planner loads the statistics, and cached, not enough?
How much do pg_statistic size, ANALYZE WAL volume and per-backend syscache memory grow against master at default and high statistics targets?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows the selectivity functions in selfuncs.c, ANALYZE and the statistics import and export code. None has spoken in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a six-slot pg_statistic layout, statistics kind 8, new pg_stats columns and the pair rules in statistics import. These cannot be removed after release.
committability.author_follow_up: Strong sign: the author posted 16 versions in two months and reported the release-build regressions without being asked.

not_now.evidence_that_would_change_it: Release-build planning-time measurements at default settings and at large statistics targets that show a net gain over master, including the default eqjoinsel() hash path. A real workload where MCV scans take a visible share of planning time would also help, together with measured catalog, WAL and syscache growth.

priority.reason: The stated target is large statistics targets with expensive comparisons, and release builds show no gain at defaults. v16 changes the catalog, views, import, pg_dump and postgres_fdw in 27 files, and the thread has not discussed a read-time sorted copy that would avoid the catalog change.

provisional_note: Only 3 of 30 messages and no code were read, so the level 2 objections on the sixth slot, the duplicated MCV data and collation version changes were not evaluated. The privilege and leakproof handling of the new paths could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add support for (Var op Var) clause in extended MCV statistics
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner use extended MCV statistics to estimate (Var op Var) clauses such as a < b, which today get a fixed default selectivity. It adds checks in clause_selectivity_ext(), statext_is_compatible_clause_internal() and mcv_get_match_bitmap() to recognize these clauses and match them against MCV items.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Tomas Vondra asked for support for expressions and for a benchmark of planning overhead with extended statistics in place, and he also asked how much the patch helps in practice. The thread does not show these requests answered in full, and no one replied to the updated patch of 2024-09-09.

precedents_retrieved.title: ANALYZE: hash-accelerate MCV tracking for equality-only types
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch speeds up compute_distinct_stats(), the ANALYZE path for types with equality but no ordering, by adding a simplehash table from tracked values to track[] slots when attstattarget >= 100. It also replaces the shift-based eviction of count=1 entries with a cursor that keeps the same FIFO order.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Ilia Evdokimov asked how often this narrow path runs, since most types use compute_scalar_stats(), and John Naylor questioned the threshold of 100. Both points were still open when the entry was withdrawn, on the day Ilia posted a cleanup review of v5 with no objection.

precedents_retrieved.title: _bt_binsrch* improvements - equal-prefix-skip binary search
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes _bt_compare and the _bt_binsrch* functions to track which key columns are already known equal from the page's high and low keys, so later comparisons skip that equal prefix during descent. It also moves the core of _bt_compare into a static inline function to cut call overhead in the binary search loops.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Geoghegan noted that his earlier patch for the same idea, dynamic prefix truncation, hit a problem with concurrent page deletions. A scan that carries a skipped prefix down the tree can land on a page that no longer shares that prefix. The author agreed this makes the approach near impossible without resetting the prefix on every page, and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Concurrent page deletions could occur, which could
cause a scan that skips a prefix to miss that the page it landed on
doesn't have the same common prefix anymore.

precedents_retrieved.title: SIMD optimization for list_sort and tuple-sort
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Heikki Linnakangas, John Naylor, Álvaro Herrera
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds list_sort_simd_float and list_sort_simd_uint32, which take an extractor function and sort list cells with the external x86-simd-sort library, with a comparator as tie-breaker. The library would be an optional build dependency, the existing list_sort stays unchanged, and pgvector's HNSW index build was the first user, with a 7-10% faster build.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers said list_sort is not performance-critical in Postgres and that a use case in one extension does not justify a new library dependency. They suggested putting the code in pgvector or targeting pg_qsort and tuple sort instead. Álvaro Herrera returned the entry with feedback, citing the shared-library concern and noting that Debian does not package x86-simd-sort. The authors then withdrew it because the original developer had left Intel and the library's future was uncertain.
matched_queries: most common values sorted by value
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Optional" and "Does not impact" are not great selling points to get us to take a 1500 line patch. As we told you in November, list_sort isn't critical for us.

precedents_retrieved.title: Provide the facility to set binary format output for specific OID's per session
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a session setting, format_binary, that lists type OIDs the server should always send in binary format, for example set format_binary='20,21,25'. Drivers such as JDBC and pgx could then get binary results without a Describe round trip, including with the simple query protocol and connection pools.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Early on, Kyotaro Horiguchi said binary format should not be turned on without regard to the peer's capability and that the Bind message already selects formats. The later visible messages are only rebase requests and the author asking for a review, and the last one is from 2022-11, about 15 months before the decision.

precedents_retrieved.title: Binary I/O for isn extension
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds binary send/receive functions for the data types of the isn extension, so binary-first clients such as Npgsql can use them. The second version bumps the extension version and adds an upgrade script that sets the new functions by updating pg_type directly, because alter type cannot add send/receive functions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying after contrib functions were marked parallel, and the author did not send a rebased version for over a month. Robert Haas marked it Returned with Feedback at the end of the commitfest. The author said he had no time for it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So, it's been over a month since this request, and there doesn't seem
to be an update to this patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add uri percent-encoding for binary data
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds 'uri' as a format for encode() and decode(), using RFC 3986 percent-encoding on binary data. The author wanted fast URL building in PL/pgSQL, for example with encode(convert_to(..., 'UTF8'), 'uri').
precedents_retrieved.objection: Daniel Gustafsson argued that the encoding ignores the URI scheme and context, so it percent-encodes delimiters such as those in https:// and the @ in userinfo, and double-encodes IPv6 zone identifiers. He suggested renaming it to 'percent-encoding' instead. The author did not send a new version addressing this feedback, and the patch no longer applied, so the entry was closed at the end of July 2020.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I agree that uri decoding/encoding would be useful, but I'm not convinced that
this patch does the functionality justice enough to be useful.

precedents_retrieved.title: WAL-logging facility for pgstats kinds
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a new "PgStat" resource manager and a pgstat_xlog_data() entry point so that any pgstats kind, including custom ones, can WAL-log its own stats data. Each kind handles replay through a redo callback in PgStat_KindInfo, so it can decide how the data persists on standbys and after crash recovery.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected that stats only make sense on a replica or after a crash when they cover changes that are already WAL-logged, so they should be rebuilt during replay from the WAL records of the underlying objects. For table stats he proposed keying relation stats by relfilenode. He repeated the objection when the entry moved to the next CF, and the author then withdrew the patch and kept it aside.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I can't think of a real case where we would want to WAL log the stats
themselves, rather than re-emitting stats during replay based on the WAL
record of the "underlying object".

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve management of SLRU statistics collection.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Improve management of SLRU statistics collection.
Reverted commit(s): Move each SLRU's lwlocks to a separate tranche.; Collect statistics about SLRU caches
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Instead of re-identifying which statistics bucket to use for a given
SLRU on every counter increment, do it once during shmem initialization.
This saves a fair number of cycles, and there's no real cost because
we could not have a bucket assignment that varies over time or across
backends anyway.

Also, get rid of the ill-considered decision to let pgstat.c pry
directly into SLRU's shared state; it's cleaner just to have slru.c
pass the stats bucket number.

In consequence of these changes, there's no longer any need to store
an SLRU's LWLock tranche info in shared memory, so get rid of that,
making this a net reduction in shmem consumption.  (That partly
reverts fe702a7b3.)

This is basically code review for 28cac71bd, so I also cleaned up
some comments, removed a dangling extern declaration, fixed some
things that should be static and/or const, etc.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent records a rejection reason that applies to value-sorted MCVs or to raising STATISTIC_NUM_SLOTS. P4 shares only the 'performance patch' theme. Message #1 builds on an earlier thread and CF entry, and message #28 cites three older discussions in support of the paired design, but the material does not say how those ended, so no prior-rejection objection can rest on them.
Objections were raised; see the list.
Physical replication, hot standby and the wire protocol are not affected. pg_upgrade carries only kind 1, and the planner falls back to it until the next ANALYZE, which looks harmless.

The proposal reorders and duplicates data that pg_stats and pg_stats_ext_exprs already expose, so it gives no role access to anything new. Message #26 drops the pg_statistic join that failed for non-superusers and keeps the views' existing filters. Message #30 makes the ordered paths depend on permission to call the actual comparator, and has import reject unsorted or kind-8-only input. Without the code I could not check four things: that the v16 view columns use the same privilege and row-security filter, that the leakproof check now covers the '<' operator used for equality lookups, that ordering validation on restore cannot be bypassed, and that the sixth slot adds no DoS path.
Objections were found, so this note does not apply.
No contrib module or extension does value-ordered MCV lookup. Histogram bounds exclude MCVs, so they do not replace the scalar fast paths. The thread settled this point (message #30).
Two objections apply. Both are 'not now, show demand' at level 1b. Release-build measurements of real workloads could change the answer.
